Declares: `FetchOptions`, `Response`, `fetch`

```luau
--- The response to a `fetch` request.
declare extern type Response with
    --- HTTP status code, e.g. 200 or 404.
    status: number

    --- The standard reason phrase for `status`, e.g. "Not Found".
    statusText: string

    --- True when `status` is in the 200-299 range.
    ok: boolean

    --- The final URL, after any redirects.
    url: string

    --- Response headers keyed by lower-case name. Repeated headers are
    --- joined with ", ".
    headers: { [string]: string }

    --- Resolves with the body as a string.
    function text(self): Promise<string>

    --- Resolves with the body as a new buffer.
    function arrayBuffer(self): Promise<buffer>

    --- One header by case-insensitive name, or nil when it is absent.
    function header(self, name: string): string?
end

--- Options for `fetch`.
export type FetchOptions = {
    --- HTTP method: GET (the default), HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE or
    --- OPTIONS.
    method: string?,
    --- Request headers. Cookie, Host, Origin, Referer, Sec-* and Proxy-*
    --- cannot be set.
    headers: { [string]: string }?,
    --- Request body. Not allowed with GET or HEAD.
    body: (string | buffer)?,
    --- Milliseconds before the request fails with "timeout". Defaults to
    --- 30000 and is capped at 60000.
    timeout: number?,
}

--- Requests an https: URL on a public host and resolves with its
--- `Response`. Requests never carry cookies or stored credentials, and the
--- host decides whether scripts may use the network at all.
---
--- Failures reject with a string "<code>: <message>", where code is one of
--- disabled, policy, rateLimited, timeout, aborted, tooLarge or network.
--- ```lua
--- async(function()
---     local ok, result = await(fetch("https://example.com/"))
---     if ok then
---         local _, body = await(result:text())
---         print(result.status, #body)
---     else
---         print("fetch failed:", result)
---     end
---     return nil
--- end)
--- ```
declare function fetch(url: string, options: FetchOptions?): Promise<Response>
